title: Knock (1879)
hookLine: a silent apparition in the rain in an Irish village

cards: It's a wet evening in a small village in the west of Ireland, and it's raining hard. A woman walking past the parish church stops.
She sees figures, she'll later say, at the gable wall, standing in a soft light a little above the grass. She runs for others. Neighbors come, old people and children.
They stand in the downpour and look, and kneel, and someone starts the rosary. The figures don't move toward them. Nobody calls out, nobody asks for anything, nobody gives a message.
People stay a long time, soaked, praying, watching. And then it's over.

teach.b: First, the silence. Lourdes had a lady who spoke to Bernadette; Fatima had requests for the children. At Knock, by the witnesses' accounts, no one spoke at all.
For a Church that has heard so many words, that's a striking thing to keep. Second, who was there. The witnesses described Mary, crowned, her hands raised and her eyes lifted, as if in prayer.
Beside her, Joseph, his head bowed toward her. On her other side, a figure they took to be John the Evangelist, dressed like a bishop and holding an open book.

And in the middle, an altar, with a cross and a lamb standing on it. Third, the lamb. In the Apocalypse, the book John is said to have written, he sees in heaven, in the Douay-Rheims, "a Lamb standing as it were slain."
For Christians, the Lamb is Christ: wounded, and alive.
Some readers see the whole vision as a picture of the Mass, with Mary, Joseph and John gathered around the altar, saying nothing, because the one in the middle is the point.
Fourth, why silence speaks. Knock was a poor village in a country that had known famine and hard years. What came wasn't a lecture or a warning.
It was company, in the rain.

teach.h: LET ALL THE EARTH KEEP SILENCE BEFORE HIM.
teach.b: The prophet Habacuc has a line for it: "But the Lord is in his holy temple: let all the earth keep silence before him." At Knock, the earth did.

how: Catholics make pilgrimages to the shrine at Knock in County Mayo, Ireland, where the gable wall of the old parish church is kept as a chapel; pilgrims pray the rosary there and come for Mass and confession.

games.q: you're kneeling in the rain at the church wall. the figures are right there. you wait for the lady to speak. what does she say?
o: a message for the whole world.
a request to build a chapel here.
games.why: nothing. by the witnesses' accounts the vision was silent. the lamb on the altar stood at the center, and the people stayed and prayed.

practice: No words today, not even inside; if a thought starts talking, let it trail off, the way a conversation stops when someone points at the sky.

Think of the people at the gable wall, kneeling in the rain, watching: you don't have to see anything, just be someone who stays. If you pray, let this be prayer without a single word in it; if not, let it be honest quiet.

wordCard.voice: Knock. The Irish village where, by the witnesses' accounts, Mary, Joseph and John stood beside an altar with a lamb, in the rain, and not one word was spoken. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: Lamb of God, sung at Mass before communion; the lamb stood at the center of the vision at Knock.
